claims.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct enforced entirely within Pulumi and is never sent to the cloud provider.

Many cloud resources carry their own separate deletion-protection attributes, such as `deletionProtection` on a GCP Cloud SQL instance or an AWS RDS instance, which the cloud provider enforces independently of Pulumi.
A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi (protect option off) and still refuse to be deleted because of provider-side deletion protection, or vice versa.

The docs page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell Pulumi protect and provider deletion protection apart and resolve each.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes, separate from Pulumi's `protect` resource option, which the provider or the cloud API enforces independently.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute (deletion protection on the resource itself).
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute (deletion protection on the resource itself).
Pulumi's `protect` resource option and a resource's own provider/cloud deletion-protection attributes are complementary rather than substitutes for one another.

The Pulumi docs page 'Destroy failures' troubleshooting has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell the two protection layers apart and resolve a destroy failure caused by either.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
The page /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/ exists and explains how to remove the `protect` resource option.
Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute, and the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` and `gcp.container.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the provider.
AWS RDS `deletionProtection`, EC2 `disableApiTermination`, and Azure Resource Manager management locks are enforced by the cloud API, independent of Pulumi.
Azure Resource Manager returns an error code such as `ScopeLocked` when deleting a resource under a management lock.
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is recorded in the stack's state, not what the program currently says, so setting the attribute to false in the program alone is not enough.
To remove provider- or cloud-enforced deletion protection: set the attribute to false in the program, run `pulumi up` to update the live resource and state, then run `pulumi destroy`.
If protection was disabled outside Pulumi, `pulumi refresh` synchronizes state with reality and `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute, and a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` guards the instance at the GCP API level.
`gcp.container.Cluster` and `gcp.bigquery.Table` have a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
`gcp.bigquery.Dataset` has a `deleteContentsOnDestroy` attribute; destroying a dataset containing tables fails unless it is true.
`aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` attribute enforced by the AWS API that defaults to false.
`aws.s3.BucketV2` has a `forceDestroy` attribute that defaults to false; a non-empty bucket otherwise fails to delete.
`aws.ec2.Instance` has a `disableApiTermination` attribute enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection).
`aws.dynamodb.Table` has a `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute enforced by the AWS API that defaults to false.

`azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and scope-specific variants such as `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel` exist; a `CanNotDelete` lock enforced by Azure Resource Manager must be removed before the resource can be deleted.

Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it; recreating a vault with the same name fails with `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered, and purge protection prevents purging until the retention period elapses.
